Series::host¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signatures¶

template<class T>
Series::HostValue<T> Series::host() const

Series::HostAny Series::host() const

The Rank-Aware Host Boundary¶

host() materializes an owning CPU representation without pretending that every Series is a flat vector. The typed overload converts every lane to T and returns HostValue<T>. The untyped overload preserves the runtime ScalarType in HostAny.

The selected payload follows rank:

Series rank

Typed state

Untyped state

Native meaning

0

is_scalar()

is_scalar()

one scalar value

1

is_vector()

is_vector()

one std::vector

2+

is_array()

is_array()

flat owning data plus sizes, strides, and contiguity

Rank—not numel()—selects the state. A shape [1] Series remains a vector, whereas shape [] is scalar. This distinction is why host() is appropriate for generic boundaries and why item() and pull() can enforce narrower contracts.

For an N-D result, array().data is contiguous row-major logical data. array().sizes records the original shape; array().strides records the source layout; and array().contiguous reports whether the source was already contiguous before materialization. Thus a transposed view exports values in logical order without falsely reporting that its source layout was dense.

Ownership, Conversion, And Autodiff¶

Every payload owns its host allocation. There is no alias back into Series storage. Device-backed values synchronize and transfer once; strided values are traversed in logical row-major order; and typed export performs the requested element conversion.

Host extraction is an observation boundary, not a differentiable operation. It neither mutates nor detaches the Series, but calculations performed on the returned C++ storage cannot contribute to reverse().

Examples¶

1. Distinguish a scalar from a singleton vector¶

const auto scalar = pluss::make_series(7).host<std::int64_t>();
const auto vector = pluss::make_series({7}).host<std::int64_t>();

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "scalar=" << scalar.is_scalar()
          << " vector=" << vector.is_vector() << '\n';

Output¶

scalar=true vector=true

Both payloads contain one value, but their ranks remain different.

2. Inspect a matrix without losing its geometry¶

const auto host =
    pluss::make_series({1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}, {2, 3})
        .host<std::int64_t>();
const auto& array = host.array();

std::cout << "shape=" << array.sizes[0] << 'x' << array.sizes[1]
          << " flat=";
for (auto value : array.data) std::cout << value << ' ';
std::cout << '\n';

Output¶

shape=2x3 flat=1 2 3 4 5 6

The flat allocation is accompanied by enough metadata to reconstruct the matrix exactly.

3. Preserve source-layout information while materializing logical order¶

const auto view =
    pluss::make_series({1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}, {2, 3}).transpose(0, 1);
const auto host = view.host<std::int64_t>();

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "shape=" << host.array().sizes[0] << 'x'
          << host.array().sizes[1]
          << " source_contiguous=" << host.array().contiguous
          << " values=";
for (auto value : host.array().data) std::cout << value << ' ';
std::cout << '\n';

Output¶

shape=3x2 source_contiguous=false values=1 4 2 5 3 6

The exported data is contiguous and logically ordered; the flag describes the receiver from which it was produced.

4. Request an explicit host element type¶

const auto host = pluss::make_series({1, 2, 3}).host<double>();
std::cout << host.array().data[0] << ' '
          << host.array().data[1] << ' '
          << host.array().data[2] << '\n';

Output¶

1 2 3

The Series dtype is unchanged; the host payload contains double values. host() does not expose a second vector-extraction method: use pull<double>() when rank one is part of the contract, and inspect array().data when generic code is already handling arbitrary rank and metadata.

5. Preserve runtime dtype with untyped export¶

const auto host = pluss::make_series({true, false}).host();
const auto& values = host.vector_as<bool>();

std::cout << host.dtype() << ' ' << std::boolalpha
          << values[0] << ' ' << values[1] << '\n';

Output¶

bool true false

Use untyped export when generic code must inspect the runtime dtype rather than choosing a conversion type at the call site.

See Also¶

  • item(): require rank zero and return one native scalar.

  • pull(): require rank one and return std::vector<T> directly.

  • sizes(): inspect shape without materializing values.

  • strides(): inspect source layout without a host transfer.

  • contiguous(): produce a dense Series while remaining in Series space.
